language.script_notes: All road signage is in English, which is the quick separator from the French-speaking neighbours (Ivory Coast, Togo, Benin). Local languages like Twi appear on shopfronts but not on official signs. .gh domain; area codes 030 Accra, 032 Kumasi, 037 Tamale.

road_furniture.bollard_color: Ghana has no common roadside bollard.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard steel W-beam on the main highways; frequently absent elsewhere.
road_furniture.line_paint: Often minimal or absent on rural roads; white centre and edge lines on trunk roads. Town kerbs are usually painted black-and-yellow.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Concrete and wooden utility poles. Look for roadside kiosks and shipping-container shops painted in telecom colours (MTN yellow, red, blue) and small lottery stands with red/yellow/green boxes.

architecture.roof_style: Low gables and lean-tos; a lot of unfinished single-storey construction.
architecture.roof_material: Corrugated metal sheeting, very often rusted to a deep brown; some concrete slabs in towns.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete or sandcrete block, frequently left unrendered and unfinished; mud brick in the rural north.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bare grey block, whitewash, and bright paint on shops and churches.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Half-finished block houses; roadside kiosks and containers used as shops; churches with painted signboards; round mud huts with thatched roofs in the far north.

nature.vegetation: The south is humid — oil palms, banana and dense forest through the cocoa belt. The north is dry savanna with scattered shrubs and bare ground. Lake Volta is a huge water body filling much of the east.
nature.terrain: Mostly low plateau and coastal plains; hillier around the Akwapim–Togo ranges in the south-east.
nature.climate_signature: Reddish laterite soil at the roadside, strongest through the centre and east. Hazy, dusty skies in the north during the Harmattan season.

vehicles.plate_color: White with black characters for private vehicles; yellow plates for taxis and commercial vehicles.
vehicles.plate_format: Two-letter region code, four digits, then a two-digit year of registration (e.g. GR 1234-23) — the year suffix is a useful dating tell.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Old Toyotas and Opels; 'trotro' minibuses, often with painted slogans on the back; yellow taxis.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: White Google car with a roof rack that has a piece of BLACK DUCT TAPE on the FRONT-right bar — the fastest way to tell Ghana from Nigeria. (If the tape is on the REAR-right, it is Réunion Island, not Ghana.)

confusion_set.shared_traits: English signage, right-hand traffic, similar unfinished block architecture, rusted metal roofs, red soil
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ghana's Google car has black tape on the FRONT-right roof-rack bar; Nigeria's car differs. Ghana plates carry a two-digit year suffix; Nigeria uses green plates with state names.

confusion_set.shared_traits: West African coast, oil palms and cocoa, red soil, right-hand traffic
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ivory Coast signage is in French; Ghana's is in English. Plate formats and the Google car also differ.

confusion_set.shared_traits: The Street View car's roof-rack tape looks almost identical
confusion_set.tiebreaker: On Réunion the tape is on the REAR-right bar, not the front. Réunion is a small mountainous French island with EU plates, euros and French signage.
